review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the helper file CompactParameterIntegral.lean and Mathlib's continuity-of-parametric-integral lemmas in DominatedConvergence.lean and Bochner/Set.lean. The smooth proofs use the project's own integral_contDiff, which already takes a ≤ b and interval-integral form, so they have no repeated Icc-conversion. The only repeated nontrivial block is in the two continuity proofs: apply the compact-set parametric-integral lemma, then convert Icc to interval-integral form. Mathlib's continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous' does this directly. The proposed rewrites have not been compiled. In particular I did not check that f.uncurry unifies definitionally with hG and hr (I expect it does), or that the volume instances (NullSingletonClass, IsLocallyFiniteMeasure) resolve automatically (also expected). The Mathlib lemma needs no FirstCountableTopology or LocallyCompactSpace on Y, so those assumptions on line 54 may become unnecessary. I did not check whether other files rely on them. I found no other worthwhile repetition. The contDiff and continuous proof pairs share only a short parallel structure, not a reusable block.

findings.problem: Both continuity proofs repeat the same three steps. (1) Apply continuous_parametric_integral_of_continuous on a compact Icc 0 c, which needs an explicit IsCompact ascription and a Continuous uncurry hypothesis. (2) State the interval-integral form separately (hi', hm'). (3) Convert Icc to Ioc and then to ∫ s in 0..c with a simpa using intervalIntegral.integral_of_le and integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc. The Icc/Ioc/interval-integral conversion is repeated, once with the constant 1 and once with P and hP. Mathlib already states continuity of a parametric interval integral directly, so the hand-written conversion is unnecessary.
findings.proposed_change:
No new local lemma is needed. Use Mathlib's `intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous'` (hf : Continuous f.uncurry) (a₀ b₀ : ℝ) in both places. In `rawPrimitive_joint_continuous`, replace lines 61–66 with
`have hi' : Continuous (fun p : Y × ℝ => ∫ s in (0:ℝ)..1, F (p.1,p.2*s)) := intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous' (μ := volume) (f := fun p : Y × ℝ => fun s : ℝ => F (p.1,p.2*s)) hG 0 1`.
In `primitive_joint_continuous`, replace lines 74–78 with
`have hm' : Continuous (fun y : Y => ∫ s in (0:ℝ)..P, rawPrimitive (fun θ => F (y,θ)) s) := intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous' (μ := volume) (f := fun y : Y => fun s : ℝ => rawPrimitive (fun θ => F (y,θ)) s) hr 0 P`.
The final lines (`simpa ... using continuous_snd.smul hi'` and `exact hr.sub ...`) stay unchanged. With these rewrites `hP` is no longer used in this proof's conversion step, and the `Icc`/`isCompact_Icc` ascriptions disappear. The theorem statements keep their hypotheses (hP) and meaning. Also check whether `[FirstCountableTopology Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y]` on line 54 can be dropped, since the Mathlib lemma only needs `TopologicalSpace`. Dropping them would generalize both theorems.
findings.benefit: This removes two copies of the compact-set to interval-integral conversion, which is the main repeated reasoning in the section. Each proof shrinks to building the uncurried continuity hypothesis plus one library call. Maintainers no longer track the Icc/Ioc/integral_of_le rewrites, and the separate hP use goes away. The section may also generalize to arbitrary topological parameter spaces.
